title: RWB-S5-E3021: the take-on step consumes and publishes an event and reads four owner contracts, while the plan carries no C or I row and its pattern set omits DP-09
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json slices RWB-S5-E3021-APP and -CON (H, C, I, X and patterns); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5, six REST operations, one event, one job, one workflow, and the slide 13 row of S5); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 3, 13, 19, 41 and 43 as quoted in the context pack and in RWB-S5-E3019-CON; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T2, T5.3, T-A.2, appendix T-B); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.3.2, A2.3.3.1, A2.3.4.4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-03; legacy RWB-E3-021
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies, Integration dependencies); Sections 2, 3, 4, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.7 and 13 of the APP slice; Sections 2, 3, 7 AC3, AC4 and AC5, 11, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.7 and 13 of the CON slice
description: (1) The plan gives both slices H = RWB-S5-E3021-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the APP slice and no dependency for the CON slice, with C, I and X empty, while the step consumes the rwb-litigation auction result, reads the rwb-source-data data product, and reads and answers rwb-case. (2) The plan's pattern set is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19, so DP-09 is absent, although the step both consumes one event and publishes one and needs the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON. (3) Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT names AssetTakenOn on rwb.asset.events.v1 with rwb-case and rwb-payment as consumers, and slide 19 IN names the events rwb-asset consumes, of which AuctionResult is the one this feature needs. (4) No source publishes an operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, so the case state read and the move answer are declared as consumed shapes with the operation name placeholder. (5) TSD S5 T5.3 lists AssetTakenOn as the only event of the module, and TSD S5 T5.1 omits the LED portal that FSD S5 A2.3.2 names as an integration point.
evidence: split_plan.json slices RWB-S5-E3021-APP (H of three CRs, empty C, I and X) and RWB-S5-E3021-CON (all four lists empty); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-05, DP-09, DP-13 and DP-19; context pack S5 slide 13 row of S5 with E in the S4 column and T E in the P8 and S9 columns; TSD S5 T5.3 'AssetTakenOn Published'; TSD S5 A2.6.3.3 and T-A.2 for the operations; legacy RWB-E3-021 AC1 to AC4
area: Dependency rows, event delivery and the case boundary, S5 rwb-asset
proposed: Keep the H, C, I and X rows exactly as the plan states them, declare the consumed AuctionResult event and the three consumed REST rows as facts with fakes on Day 1, and record RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as the wave 0 outbox and inbox library the step needs

title: RWB-S5-E3021: two of the four legacy criteria are the rules of the other take-on routes and the LED rule of the feature has no legacy criterion
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-021, Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3, Test cases TC-E3-021-02 and TC-E3-021-03); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md headings RWB-E3-019 and RWB-E3-020 (their AC2 and AC3); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1 and A2.3.3.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-01, R-DIS-02 and R-DIS-03; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T4
description: FEAT-AST-03 is the LED auction take-on and its rule is R-DIS-03 (ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON, LED_HANDOVER_RECEIVED, led_result = handed_over, to ASSET_ON_BOOKS). The legacy story of RWB-E3-021 instead carries AC2 'Rule R-DIS-01' (the vehicle repossession of FEAT-AST-01) and AC3 'Rule R-DIS-02' (the deed in lieu transfer of FEAT-AST-02), and the same two criteria appear again in RWB-E3-019 and RWB-E3-020, so three APP stories of this service own overlapping words while the rule of their own feature has no criterion. The criteria cannot be reworded, so the behaviour must be built once and the duplication must be resolved by a component rule rather than by a second implementation.
evidence: legacy RWB-E3-021 AC2 'Given a case in state ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON / When repossession completed' and AC3 'When dil transfer registered'; the same lines in RWB-E3-019 AC2 and RWB-E3-020 AC2 and AC3; FSD S5 A2.3.3.1 which gives FEAT-AST-03 the rules R-DIS-01, R-DIS-02, R-DIS-03 and BR-S5-003; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-01 to R-DIS-03; TSD S5 T4 rows R-DIS-01, R-DIS-02 and R-DIS-03 with distinct events
area: Acceptance criteria and rule ownership, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: Business analyst with the S5 service owner
proposed: Copy all four legacy criteria verbatim, build one shared take-on component that serves R-DIS-01, R-DIS-02 and R-DIS-03, let RWB-S5-E3019-APP and RWB-S5-E3020-APP prove R-DIS-01 and R-DIS-02, and cover R-DIS-03 here with one new criterion and one new test case

title: RWB-S5-E3021: the LED result, its event properties, its column and the rwb-litigation contract have no published shape
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: two tables asset_sale and listing, no asset row; one event EV-22; the slide 13 row of S5); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset, T3.2 lists, T4 DISPOSAL, T5.1 external interfaces, T5.3 events, appendix T-A); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.3.2 integration points, A2.3.3.1 rules, A2.6.3.2 field catalog); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-AST-03 row); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-03; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 19, 29, 37 and 45 as quoted in the context pack and in RWB-S5-E3019-CON; legacy RWB-E3-021 Data table
description: (1) The take-on of a property after an LED auction must record the LED result, the round and the ladder of 100, 90, 80 then 70 percent, and the asset table of TSD S5 T3.1 has no column, no list and no value for any of them; the only column that can carry the auction money is auction_purchase_price (DF-COL-038). (2) The ownership rows of S5 carry one event, EV-22, and no consumed event, so the inbound AuctionResult of slide 19 IN has no property list, no consumer group and no deduplication rule in any module source. (3) The producer of the LED result is not named in any ownership row: FSD S5 A2.3.2 names the LED portal as an integration point, TSD S5 T5.1 lists SVAF, AMIS, RPS and HOME.SCB only, and the legacy story depends on FEAT-LIT-19, so the story key of the rwb-litigation contract that answers the auction result is not published. (4) The asset record itself has no Ownership Map row although Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1 give it to S5, and the record links to the ACE asset by asset_key while the asset table has no asset_key column.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset columns DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 (no led_result, no round, no ladder column; auction_purchase_price DF-COL-038); TSD S5 T3.2 lists LOV-ASSET-TYPE, LOV-HOLDING, LOV-LISTING, LOV-SALE-CHANNEL, LOV-SEGMENT and LOV-TRANSFER-IN with no LED list; TSD S5 T5.1 INT-11 to INT-27 with no LED interface; TSD S5 T5.3 'AssetTakenOn Published' only; context pack S5 ownership rows 'Events (1) EV-22'; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-AST-03 'Links the case to the property in v_ace_npa_asset ... by asset_key'; TSD S5 A2.6.3.2 'v_ace_npa_asset.asset_key ... link to it by key, no foreign key'
area: Data model, event shape and external interface, S5 rwb-asset
owner_role: Solution architect and the business analyst of S5
proposed: Consume the LED handover as the rwb-litigation AuctionResult event, carry the LED result, the round and the ladder as event facts and decision-record facts, write the handover price to DF-COL-038, use asset_ref as the asset-key link with no foreign key, and carry the event property names and the producer story key as placeholders until the owner publishes them

title: RWB-S5-E3021: the legacy key and both slices carry no requirement id and TSD S5 T8 names none for FEAT-AST-03
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-021, metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices, empty); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (requirements served); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-AST-03 row)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both slices; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The traceability of both slices needs one sourced requirement. The legacy story master of RWB-E3-021 carries no requirement id, the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, and TSD S5 T8 names REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only, with no row for FEAT-AST-03. The only requirement of the program that names the outcome of the step is REQ-S5-001, every repossessed or surrendered asset is recorded with its source, date taken in, holding cost and provision step, which does not name an auction purchase but is the record this story creates, so both slices trace to it and the empty plan list is recorded rather than filled with an invented identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E3-021 gives Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only; the plan rows of RWB-S5-E3021-APP and RWB-S5-E3021-CON carry reqs as an empty list; TSD S5 T8 lists REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 against FEAT-AST-01 and REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-08, with 'Written one epic ahead' in the story column
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both slices to REQ-S5-001 and FEAT-AST-03 and let step D1 update the plan reqs list and the RTM rather than adding an identifier no source carries

title: RWB-S5-E3021: the FSD S5 and the TSD S5 that both slices read are In review with an empty sign-off table and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 / Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature table); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; Sections 3 of both slices
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S5 is at version 3, 15 November 2026, with status In review and an empty sign-off table, and the TSD S5 is at version 2, 28 October 2026, with status In review and an empty sign-off table, and the run of D-RCV-60 has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed. The release date 31 January 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
evidence: FSD S5 document control gives Status In review, Date 15 November 2026, and its document sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells; TSD S5 document control gives Status In review, Date 28 October 2026, and its sign-off table is empty; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of S5
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status changes
